description: The bar chart illustrates the accuracy (%) of a multimodal misinformation detection model under various ablation conditions, comparing performance on two datasets: one unnamed (left group) and “PolitiFact” (right group). The vertical axis represents accuracy from 75.0% to 95.0%, with major gridlines at 0.5% intervals. Each group contains six bars corresponding to different model variants: “Ours” (full model), “w/o comments”, “w/o text”, “w/o select”, “w/o emotion”, and “w/o cognition”. In the left group, “Ours” achieves 89.84%, followed by “w/o comments” at 86.82%, “w/o text” at 80.10%, “w/o select” at 88.80%, “w/o emotion” at 87.34%, and “w/o cognition” at 87.17%. In the “PolitiFact” group, “Ours” reaches 90.57%, “w/o comments” 85.85%, “w/o text” 83.02%, “w/o select” 89.62%, “w/o emotion” 84.91%, and “w/o cognition” 87.74%. The bars are color-coded: dark red for “Ours”, orange for “w/o comments”, yellow for “w/o text”, light blue for “w/o select”, medium blue for “w/o emotion”, and dark blue for “w/o cognition”. A gray horizontal bar near the top (around 93.5%) appears to be a reference or baseline, though unlabeled. The chart visually demonstrates that removing text has the most detrimental effect on performance, while the full model (“Ours”) consistently outperforms all ablated versions on both datasets.
